docRequirement: hooks.md § StopFailure input (:2291-2297, example :2299-2307) binds the StopFailure hook input to three event-specific fields on top of the common ones: `error` — "Error type: `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, or `unknown`", and "The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering"; optional `error_details` — "Additional details about the error, when available"; and optional `last_assistant_message`, which for StopFailure "contains the API error string itself, such as `\"API Error: Rate limit reached\"`" rather than the assistant's text. Per § Hook input, for command hooks that JSON object is what arrives on stdin.

divergence: Payload only — matcher filtering already conforms. Three deltas: (1) the documented field `error` is absent; what we ship is `error_code`, and it is not merely a key rename — the value is the unprojected Nessy `ErrorCode` (`rate_limited`, `service_error`, `invalid_model`), whereas `error` is documented to carry the projected vocabulary (`rate_limit`, `server_error`, `model_not_found`). The projection table that does exactly this mapping already exists at packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:126-142 but is applied only to the match value. So the fix is rename + project, not rename alone. (2) `error_details` has no producer and no field on `SdkAutomationInput`, even though `AgentError.originalError` / `.details` are in hand at every emit site. (3) `last_assistant_message` is documented for StopFailure as the rendered API error string; we emit it for Stop/SubagentStop only, never for StopFailure, and the rendered error text (`AgentError.title`/`.message`, or `errorObj.message` at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6804) is discarded before the emit.

change.what: Widen the parameter from `errorCode: string` to the error object already available at the call sites (`Pick<AgentError, 'code' | 'title' | 'message' | 'originalError' | 'details'>`, or `{ code, renderedText, details }`). Emit, at :7322: `error: toDocumentedStopFailureError(code)` (the projected documented value), KEEP `error_code: code.slice(0, 64)` unchanged for existing native automations, add `error_details` from `originalError ?? details?.join('; ')` when present (bound it — the current 64-char slice is too short for a detail string; 1024 is the natural cap, matching how other free-text payload fields are treated), and add `last_assistant_message` = the rendered error text (`title`/`message`, e.g. `API Error: <title>`), NOT `this.lastAssistantMessageText` — hooks.md:2297 says this field is the error string for StopFailure. Emit both `error` and `error_code`: the matcher reads `input.error_code ?? input.error` (utils.ts:215) so carrying both leaves every existing matcher byte-identical.

Pass the error object instead of `.code`: `this.emitStopFailureHookOnce(event.error)` at :6760, `this.emitStopFailureHookOnce(typedError)` at :6800, and at :6803 pass `typedError` plus the rendered text `errorObj.message` that :6804 yields to the user — that is the string the doc's `last_assistant_message` describes for the unknown-error branch.

Export the projection as a one-line helper (`STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR[code] ?? code`) and have both the emitter and the matcher case at :214-217 call it, so the payload and the match value can never disagree. The matcher case body is otherwise unchanged.

Add `error_details?: string;` beside `error_code?` (:870) with the doc sentence as its comment, and extend the `last_assistant_message` doc comment (:873-898) with the StopFailure exception from hooks.md:2297. Update the contract row at :70 to `redactedPayload: ['error', 'error_code', 'error_details', 'last_assistant_message']`. This row is descriptive inventory — no runtime consumer reads `redactedPayload`.

Two cases, table-driven with the existing Stop payload tests (:401-443 are the model): positive — a `rate_limited` failure emits `error: 'rate_limit'`, `error_code: 'rate_limited'`, an `error_details` string and a `last_assistant_message` holding the rendered error text; boundary — a Nessy-only code with no documented counterpart (e.g. `mcp_unreachable`) passes through unchanged on BOTH keys, and `error_details`/`last_assistant_message` are absent rather than empty when the error carries no detail.

Add one row proving the payload's new shape still matches — `{ hook_event_name: 'StopFailure', error: 'rate_limit', error_code: 'rate_limited' }` against matcher `rate_limit` — so the `error_code ?? error` precedence is pinned now that both keys are present.

blastRadius: Crosses a process/trust boundary, which is the risk trigger here: the object changed is the hook stdin JSON, read by imported Claude-plugin hooks and native command automations, and it is also mirrored into the child process env as `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:53). Adding `error` starts populating `NESSY_ERROR` (hook-command.ts:64) on StopFailure for the first time — a behaviour change for any existing automation that treats `$NESSY_ERROR` as a tool-failure-only signal. One payload builder serves both execution authorities (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:737 direct spawn; packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488 sandboxed runner), and packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.plugin-hook-runners.test.ts:189 asserts that call textually, so the shared builder must not change signature. Matcher path: packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:214-217 (unchanged behaviour by construction, `error_code` still read first) and its tests packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:636-639. Type row: `AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:38-100) is re-exported across a package boundary as `PI_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_CONTRACTS` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:25) and pinned by packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.test.ts (which asserts only InstructionsLoaded's `redactedPayload`, at :172, plus StopFailure's `kind` at :163). Codex and Nestor Cloud backends emit no StopFailure at all (packages/shared/src/agent/codex-agent.ts:614-621, packages/shared/src/agent/nestor-cloud-agent.ts:286-292), a separate and larger gap this change does not touch.
userImpact: A user installs a Claude Code plugin whose StopFailure hook alerts on API failures — the documented recipe reads `input=$(cat)` then `jq -r .error` / `.error_details` / `.last_assistant_message`. On a rate-limited or auth-failed turn the hook does fire, and matcher filtering picks the right hook, but all three reads return null: the Slack/log line the user gets is empty where the error type and text should be, so they learn a turn failed and nothing about why. The same holds for a native Nessy command automation on StopFailure using `$NESSY_ERROR`, which is unset for this event while it is populated for PostToolUseFailure. Only Nessy's own Pi/native backend is affected; with NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE on, the Claude SDK supplies the fields itself.
